title: Lesson 3: Prayer
description: Prayer is talking with a Father who loves to listen. This lesson walks through the six-step pattern Jesus gave in the Lord's Prayer and helps you build your own daily prayers.

blocks.text: In the last lesson you saw that God gave you new life and adopted you into His family. Sons and daughters talk with their father. That is what prayer is, and in this lesson you will learn the pattern Jesus gave for it.

blocks.alt: A disciple watches from the pre-dawn shadow as first light breaks over the valley onto Jesus praying beside an olive tree

blocks.title: Teach Us to Pray
blocks.text:
The disciples watched Jesus pray. He got up while it was still dark and went to quiet places to talk with His Father (Mark 1:35). Before the day began, Jesus brought it to His Father, ready to do whatever His Father wanted. Prayer displayed His close relationship with the Father.

One day, when He finished praying, one of His disciples asked Him for help: "Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples" (Luke 11:1).
What is Prayer?

Even the disciples had to learn to pray, so you can too. Prayer is a conversation: talking with God and listening to Him. It shows that you depend on a powerful and loving Father. Because of Jesus, you do not come to God as a stranger hoping He will notice you. You come as His child. Prayer is talking with a Father who loves to listen.
For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!"
3.1 - How would you describe your prayer life right now?
The Pattern Jesus Gave
Jesus gave His disciples a pattern for prayer. You can find it in Matthew 6:9-13 and Luke 11:2-4.
The prayer moves in six simple steps. You do not have to pray them perfectly or word for word. Think of them as six rooms you walk through with your Father.
STEP 1 - CONNECT RELATIONALLY
"Our Father, who is in heaven"
God adopted you as His child, and He loves to hear you call Him Father. Starting with who He is to you sets the tone for everything else you pray.
3.2 - Why is it important to begin your prayers being reminded that God is your Father?
STEP 2 - WORSHIP HIS NAME
"Holy is your name"
Before you ask for anything, tell God what is true about Him. Try naming one thing: He is faithful, He is holy, He is near.
STEP 3 - PRAY HIS AGENDA FIRST
"your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven"
Children care about what their Father cares about. Before your own list, pray for His kingdom to come and His will to be done in your home, your city, and the world.
3.3 - What is one thing God cares about that you can pray for?
STEP 4 - DEPEND ON HIM FOR EVERYTHING
"Give us this day our daily bread."
God invites you to bring Him your needs, big and small, and to trust Him to provide. Nothing is too small to pray about.
3.4 - What are some needs you can ask God for today?
STEP 5 - FORGIVE AND BE FORGIVEN
"Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us."
Through Jesus, God has forgiven you completely. When you receive His forgiveness, it becomes easier to forgive the people who have hurt you.
STEP 6 - ENGAGE IN SPIRITUAL WARFARE
"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."

There is real evil in the world, and an enemy who wants to pull you away from God. Ask your Father to keep you from temptation and protect you. You pray from a safe place, because Jesus has already won.
This Week's Practice

You just walked through the six steps of the Lord's Prayer. Now make it personal. Turn the pattern into your own daily prayers: for yourself, your family, your church, and people who do not yet know Jesus. Your prayers are saved on your device so you can come back to them each day.

blocks.title: Build Your Daily Prayers
blocks.description: Use the Lord's Prayer as a pattern to create your own personalized daily prayers. Add the people and needs that are on your heart right now.

blocks.text: Each day this week, pray through your six steps once, even if it only takes five minutes. Use your own words, and start with "Father." If you forget a day or your mind wanders, do not quit. Your Father is not keeping score. Just begin again.
Lesson 3 Review

Prayer is talking with a Father who loves to listen. Jesus gave His disciples, and you, a pattern that touches every part of life: connect with your Father, worship His name, pray His agenda first, depend on Him, forgive and be forgiven, and stand against the enemy. Start putting that pattern into practice this week.
In the next lesson, you will learn how God speaks to you through the Bible.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 7, 8, and 9
blocks.intro: In John 7-9, Jesus continues to challenge what people think they know about God and about who He is. You will see Him defend a woman caught in her worst moment and restore sight to a man who had never seen. Pay attention to what these moments reveal about the character of Jesus.

blocks.text: Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What have you learned about God and yourself recently in your Daily Devotions?
What is a prayer request for this week?

retiredQuestions.text: 3.3 - What are some names and attributes of God you can proclaim in your prayers to honor Him?
